description:
We are MANDACARU by LAMIT, a team from Salvador, Brazil, tackling challenge #7 Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data. Our focus is smallholder farming in Bahia: we want to use NASA satellite data to help farmers and rural extension technicians test crop rotations with low risk and see the results on their own land.

We also bring hackathon experience, with 3 podium finishes in 2026.
summary:
Mandacaru is a decision-support platform designed to help farmers in Brazil’s Western Bahia region plan crop rotations after soybean harvest. It combines NASA Earth observation data, climate indicators, vegetation history, soil information, crop characteristics, and farmer priorities to compare rotation strategies under dry, average, and wet scenarios.

By evaluating potential benefits, costs, risks, and operational constraints, Mandacaru helps farmers understand which alternatives may be more suitable for their fields and conditions. Instead of providing generic recommendations, the platform makes relevant information easier to interpret and compare, supporting more informed agricultural decisions.

Our goal is to reduce uncertainty in crop rotation planning, improve resource allocation, and contribute to more resilient and sustainable farming systems.
details:
Mandacaru is an agricultural decision-support platform focused on one of the most important decisions in crop management: what to plant after soybean harvest.

The project was developed in response to the challenges faced by farmers in Western Bahia, Brazil, where changing rainfall patterns, higher temperatures, shorter rainy seasons, soil conditions, nematode pressure, and operational constraints make crop rotation planning increasingly complex.

Mandacaru processes Earth observation and climate data to characterize agricultural conditions and support the comparison of different crop rotation strategies. Its approach combines:

  • Earth observation data: MODIS and Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) to analyze vegetation history and post-harvest land conditions.
  • Climate information: NASA POWER and GPM IMERG to assess temperature and precipitation patterns.
  • Agronomic information: soil conditions, crop characteristics, and nematode-related information.
  • Farmer priorities: operational constraints, available machinery, costs, and production goals.

The platform compares strategies under dry, average, and wet climate scenarios, presenting their potential benefits, costs, risks, and limitations. For example, different cover crops may offer advantages in soil coverage or nematode management while also presenting specific agronomic trade-offs.

Mandacaru is designed to support farmers directly, while also serving as a tool for agricultural consultants who assist them. It does not replace agronomic expertise; instead, it helps users evaluate alternatives with more context and transparency.

The project's creative approach lies in transforming publicly available Earth observation data into practical information for a specific agricultural decision. Rather than simply displaying satellite imagery, Mandacaru connects environmental indicators with crop rotation planning and farm-level priorities.

Our intended impact is to help farmers make better-informed decisions, allocate resources more efficiently, reduce avoidable risks, and build more resilient agricultural systems.

The project was developed using React, TypeScript, Nest.js, Python, FastAPI, Postgree and Powered by NASA.
